newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Cotton seen stable in Pakistan, India range-bound.
newsitem.headline: Cotton seen stable in Pakistan, India range-bound.

text.p: Cotton prices are likely to remain stable in Pakistan on an expected delay in the arrival of 1997/98 (July-June) crop and range-bound in neighbouring India on low demand and supply, dealers in the two countries said on Friday.
In Pakistan, demand picked up this week on stable yarn prices and mill owners went for some fresh buying, dealers said.
They said exporters also showed buying interest in low quality stocks.
Prices slipped slightly this week from the previous week as panic gripped ginners who had large unsold stocks from the 1996/97 crop, the dealers said.
"Selling pressure brought the prices down and most deals were made on credit," dealer Khushi Ram said.
Pakistan's cotton output reached 8.73 million bales in 1996/97 and there is 1.508 million bales of unsold stocks available," the state Cotton Export Corporation said.

"But now cotton rates are likely to remain stable in the next couple of weeks because the new crop arrival will be delayed owing to recent rains," dealer Adil Usman said. "The new crop is expected to arrive in the market in mid-July."

In India, cotton prices are expected to remain steady, moving in a narrow range, in the current week on limited demand and supply, traders there said.
"Cotton demand from yarn mills has been very dull. But the prices are steady because quality cotton is not available," one trader said.

The bulk of the 1996/97 (October/September) crop, estimated at 16 million bales (170 kg) has already arrived in the market and "whatever is left with farmers and traders will come in small lots as and when prices firm up further," he said.

In the week to Wednesday, prices of most Indian cotton varieties remained more or less steady. Bengaldeshi was quoted at 860/920 rupees per maund (32.37 kgs) and Punjab saw-ginned was offered at 1,560/1,590.
Gujarat Kalyan was quoted at 13,200 rupees per candy (355.56 kg). Gujarat Wagad was steady at 12,600 rupees per candy.
